paper_metadata.title: Influence of Ru addition on microstructure and stress-rupture property of Ni-based single crystal superalloys
paper_metadata.journal: Progress in Natural Science: Materials International

evidence.quote: The effects of Ru on the microstructure and stress-rupture property were investigated in two experimental Ni-based single crystal superalloys with and without Ru addition (5.1%, mass fraction).
Two experimental alloys, designated USTB-F2 and USTB-F5, were directionally solidified as cylindrical single crystal bars with 14 mm in diameter and 150 mm in length.

mechanisms.name: lattice misfit effect on gamma prime morphology

evidence.quote: The changes of γ′ morphology and Re partitioning ratio as well as the partitioning behavior of Ru show good agreement with the change of the lattice misfit (Table 3).

high temperature creep and stress-rupture property of Ni-based single crystal superalloys were influenced by Ru addition in these following factors, su ch as volume fraction of γ′ precipitates, γ/γ′ lattice misfit, rafting behavior during creep, γ channel width, degree of solid solution strengthening and microstructural stability.

Assuming μ=48.2 GPa and b=0.254 nm[20−21], the uniaxial applied stresses required for bowing dislocations through the matrix channel are 318 MPa and 258 MPa in the dendrite core and interdendritic region of alloys USTB-F2, respectively, taking into account a [001] Schmid factor of 0.408. And they were 544 MPa and 395 MPa in the dendrite core and interdendritic region of alloys USTB-F5, respectively.

evidence.quote: However, alloy USTB-F5 rafted sign ificantly. And very limited secondary precipitates, marked by arrows, were observed in the dendrite core of alloy USTB-F5 (Fig.2(b)).
The changes of γ′ morphology and Re partitioning ratio as well as the partitioning behavior of Ru show good agreement with the change of the lattice misfit (Table 3).

high temperature creep and stress-rupture property of Ni-based single crystal superalloys were influenced by Ru addition in these following factors, su ch as volume fraction of γ′ precipitates, γ/γ′ lattice misfit, rafting behavior during creep, γ channel width, degree of solid solution strengthening and microstructural stability.

In this study, the γ channels in both dendrite core and interdendritic region of alloy USTB-F5 were narrower than that of alloy USTB-F2 (Fig.1 and Table 2). Assuming μ=48.2 GPa and b=0.254 nm[20−21], the uniaxial applied stresses required for bowing dislocations through the matrix channel are 318 MPa and 258 MPa in the dendrite core and interdendritic region of alloys USTB-F2, respectively, taking into account a [001] Schmid factor of 0.408. And they were 544 MPa and 395 MPa in the dendrite core and interdendritic region of alloys USTB-F5, respectively.

Ru addition im proves the stress-rupture life at 1 100 °C/140 MPa significantly due to higher γ′ volume fraction, more negative lattice misfit and a well rafting structure as well as less γ channel width.

evidence.quote: The average stress-rupture life of Ru-free alloy USTB-F2 was 73.0 h. And the average stress-rupture life of Ru- containing alloy USTB-F5 was 176.4 h, which was 2.4 times that of alloy USTB-F2.
Therefore, the Orowan resistance of alloy USTB-F5 was higher than that of alloy USTB-F2.
